Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
The test `isUnixSymlinkIsFalseIfMoreThanOneFlagIsSet()` verifies that a zip entry "META-INF/maven/" with invalid Unix permissions (having more than one flag set) does not report itself as a Unix symlink. The check for symlinks in `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()` simply calls `getUnixMode()` and checks if the unix mode bit flag masked by `UnixStat.LINK_FLAG` matches that flag exactly.

The method `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()` returns true if `(getUnixMode() & UnixStat.LINK_FLAG) == UnixStat.LINK_FLAG`. The `getUnixMode()` returns the top 16 bits of the external attributes if the platform is Unix, or 0 otherwise. The Unix stat `LINK_FLAG` is defined as an octal 0120000 (a bit mask for symbolic link file type in Unix file mode).

The bug arises when more than one bit is set in the unix mode including `LINK_FLAG`. If there is a combination of flags (e.g. mode 177777 in octal as reported in the issue), the current implementation returns true because it only checks if the `LINK_FLAG` bit is set, regardless of other bits. Therefore, if any other flags are set alongside `LINK_FLAG`, the entry may be incorrectly considered a symlink.

The test ensures that an entry with multiple flags (not a valid symlink mode) returns false, but the current implementation passes incorrectly by returning true, revealing the flaw.

The root cause is that `isUnixSymlink()` should ensure the unix mode exactly corresponds to the symlink flag, not just that bitwise `LINK_FLAG` is present. It should verify no other bits that override or contradict the symlink file type are set.

The current bug report matches this diagnosis showing `isUnixSymlink` incorrectly returns true for invalid entries having mode 177777 (all bits set). Hence the cause relates to overly permissive checking in `ZipArchiveEntry.isUnixSymlink()`.

No relevant information from recent unrelated reports.

Next, it would be good to see any more context or comments on `isUnixSymlink()` or constants in `UnixStat` that might help suggest the correct fix or intended usage.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
